scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20); has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Repository is a partial OSGeo4W-style portable QGIS install tree for Windows (201 tracked files: ~54 .bat, 4 .ps1, 4 .py, ini/json/txt config, a 44 MB data.gpkg, QGIS profile ini files, PROJ data files). Languages are mostly Batch and PowerShell, which are out of scope for skill version 1.0: full interface, data-access and secret-flow detection for those languages was not performed; only file inventory, grep-based secret patterns, config files and the Python helper (tools/validate_runtime.py) were reviewed. A non-standard 'cpp' key was added under dependencies for qgis/vcpkg/vcpkg.json. The QGIS binaries themselves are not in the repo. Installed QGIS data (data.gpkg) was not opened beyond confirming it is a SQLite 3 file. Tracked files containing absolute paths with the author's Windows user name: bin/qgis-bin.env, .claude/settings.local.json, .vscode/settings.json, portable/TODO.md (pasted assistant chat transcript).

gitignore_gaps: No .gitignore at all: .env, *.pem, *.key, credentials files, logs (var/log/setup.log.full) and local assistant settings (.claude/settings.local.json) are not excluded

findings: tools/validate_runtime.py uses only the standard library; no Python manifest exists
Bundled Python 3.12 and ~30 python3-* packages are installed via OSGeo4W (see etc/preremove and etc/postinstall .bat files) but are not pinned in a manifest in this repo

vcpkg.json uses minimum-version constraints (gdal>=3.2.0, proj>=8.0.0, qt>=6.0.0, python>=3.12.0, boost>=1.75.0) with a gdal override of 3.4.0; qt>=6.0.0 does not match the PyQt5/qt5 packages present in etc/preremove

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: os.environ.get('QGIS_ROOT') for a path setting (not a secret)

sql_injection_risk.reason: Tracked 44 MB GeoPackage data file; no code in the repo queries it

file_system_access.detail: rewrites generated environment files (bin/qgis-bin.env), makes .bak copies and writes logs under the install tree via Set-Content/Copy-Item/Out-File
same reinitialization workflow without prompts; calls bin/textreplace.exe to regenerate scripts with absolute paths
checks presence of required files under the QGIS root
hardcoded absolute paths under C:\Users\<author>\DOWNLO~1\QGIS_O~1 (machine-specific generated file, tracked)

sensitive_data_indicators.field_or_variable: password (QGIS profile setting 'password=' empty values for xyz connections; 'using-generated-random-password=true')

what_this_app_can_do: Provides a copied/portable Windows QGIS installation tree plus scripts that regenerate embedded absolute paths after the tree is moved (reinitialize via PowerShell and bin/textreplace.exe).
Ships QGIS user profiles (default, Viewer, Viewer2) with plugin repository and basemap tile connection settings.
Includes a Python validator that checks the tree for required runtime files.

data_sources_touched.source: QGIS plugin repository (plugins.qgis.org), QGIS news feed (feed.qgis.org), OpenStreetMap tiles, Mapzen terrain tiles on s3.amazonaws.com (configured in QGIS profile ini)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Desktop software run locally by whoever copies the tree; no network listener or authentication layer exists in the repo's own code.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: No secrets found, but tracked files embed the author's Windows user name and local directory layout (bin/qgis-bin.env, .claude/settings.local.json, .vscode/settings.json, portable/TODO.md).
Without a .gitignore, nothing prevents credentials, logs or assistant settings from being committed.
QGIS profile ini files configure outbound requests to public plugin, news and tile services.

top_findings: Machine-specific absolute paths with the author's Windows user name committed (bin/qgis-bin.env, .claude/settings.local.json, .vscode/settings.json)
Batch/PowerShell content is out of scope for skill v1.0; only inventory and pattern checks were run
No hardcoded secrets or secret-shaped files found
